sweep.sentence: Let us start with what Compy can already see about this PC.

crashInGame.sentence: Windows writes down every crash and freeze. Compy reads that record back in plain English and tells you what it actually says.

crashAnytime.sentence: You said it crashes any time. That could be a game, Windows, a driver or a part, so Compy starts with what Windows recorded instead of guessing.

crashBoot.sentence: Trouble right after startup is worth checking against what loads with Windows. The record names what happened last.

crashUnsure.sentence: That is fine — you do not have to know. Windows keeps the record either way, and Compy reads it for you.

slowAlways.sentence: You said it is slow all the time. That is worth checking across the whole PC, not one game at a time.

slowSometimes.sentence: You said some games are slow and others are not. That can come from a game's settings, a heavier game needing more headroom, or something else. Measured sessions are where Compy starts to answer that.

stutter.sentence: Hitching is a worst-frames problem, not an average-FPS one — the average can look perfectly fine while it is happening. So Compy compares your latest session of the game with your last steady one, and shows any crash Windows recorded.
stutter.sentenceNoCompare: Hitching is a worst-frames problem, not an average-FPS one — the average can look perfectly fine while it is happening. Sometimes a hitch is something crashing in the background, so the first check is whether Windows recorded one.

slowUnsure.sentence: No problem. The quickest way to turn a feeling into an answer is to measure it once and look at the numbers.

heat.sentence: Heat and fan noise track the same thing: how hard the parts are working, and how well the case moves air.

didItHelp.sentenceTested: Compy already measured some changes before and after on this PC. Here is what each one did to your game.
didItHelp.sentenceSince: Compy has not measured a change before and after yet, so it cannot say whether one helped. It can line up what changed and when, which shows timing, not cause.
didItHelp.sentenceUnread: Compy couldn't read its test records just now, so it can't say here whether it has measured a change. What Compy tested reads them itself.
didItHelp.sentenceUnreadSince: Compy couldn't read its test records just now, so it can't say here whether it has measured a change. It can still line up what changed and when, which shows timing, not cause.
didItHelp.sentenceUnavailableSince: Before-and-after testing is off on this PC, so Compy has no measured answer here. It can still line up what changed and when, which shows timing, not cause.

wantFps.sentence: Compy can test that on this PC: one session as it is now, one with a single change, and the change stays only if your game measured better.
wantFps.sentenceNoJourney: Compy can show you the safe changes it knows about. It has not measured them on your game, so any gain is expected, not proven.

wantMonitor.sentence: Compy can put your frame rate on screen while you play and keep a summary of the run, so “it felt smoother” becomes a number you can check.

wantScores.sentence: A benchmark is one repeatable run. Its value is comparison — the same run before and after a change tells you whether the change was real.

wantSpecs.sentence: Compy reads your parts from Windows and the drivers, and says plainly what it could not read rather than guessing.

psu.role: Feeds steady power to every part, and your power settings decide how hard they can push.

tweaks.0: Ultimate / High-performance power plan — lets parts stay at high clocks
tweaks.1: Fast Startup off — a true clean boot, not a half-hibernated state
tweaks.2: USB selective-suspend & PCIe power-saving off — no power naps mid-game

psu.tie: Prove the clocks hold with benchmarks in the Test tab.
psu.note: Compy can't read your PSU model in software, so it stays a faint placeholder — but the power settings above decide how hard everything is allowed to draw.

storage.role: Holds Windows and your games, and streams level data to the game as you play.
storage.affects: Load times and texture/streaming hitches when the game pulls data from the drive.

tweaks.0: SysMain (Superfetch) tuned so it isn't churning the disk in the background
tweaks.1: Reserved storage & free-space cleanup — keep the system drive breathing room
tweaks.2: On an HDD, Compy flags an SSD upgrade as the single biggest win (advisory)

storage.tie: Apply or undo these in the Optimize tab — all in the ledger.
storage.tieGround: Apply or undo these at Test's Optimize station — all in the ledger.

gpu.role: Renders every frame you see — the heart of your frame rate.
gpu.affects: FPS and frame consistency, especially at higher resolutions and settings.

tweaks.0: Hardware-accelerated GPU Scheduling — lets the GPU manage its own work
tweaks.1: Vendor background/telemetry services off (NVIDIA Container · AMD UXP)
tweaks.2: Force games onto your discrete GPU, and keep the driver current

gpu.tie: Watch the frames these earn you, live, in the Live tab.

cpu.role: Runs game logic, physics, and the draw calls that feed your GPU.
cpu.affects: 1% lows and frametime smoothness — steady vs. stuttery, even at the same average FPS.

tweaks.0: A power plan that lets cores boost instead of idling low
tweaks.1: Fewer startup apps fighting for CPU time (Compy's startup review)

cpu.tie: The Check tab scans for CPU limiters and applies the top fix.
cpu.tieMerged: Optimize scans for CPU limiters and applies the top fix.
cpu.tieGround: Test scans for CPU limiters and applies the top fix.
cpu.note: One honest gap: reading CPU temperature directly needs something installed deep inside Windows, and Compy ships nothing of the kind. If you run HWiNFO or LibreHardwareMonitor, Compy reads the temperature they already publish — Health shows you how.

ram.role: Keeps the game and Windows instantly on hand while you play.
ram.affects: Stutter and alt-tab hitches when free memory runs low.

tweaks.0: Compy watches memory headroom and flags heavy background apps
tweaks.1: More capacity is the real fix when a game wants more than you have (advisory)
